subject: Archaeology
title: Spears, Traps, and Hunting Strategies
description: A quick win: understand Spears, Traps, and Hunting Strategies.

hook.text: Wooden spears from 400,000 years ago were found in a German coal mine — they were sharpened, balanced, and deadly.

buildup.text: The Schöningen spears were found alongside butchered horse bones. Hunters ambushed herds at a lakeside.

discovery.text: The spears are as long as modern javelins and weighted for throwing. These were designed weapons, not sharpened sticks.

twist.text: This was 200,000 years before Homo sapiens appeared. Homo heidelbergensis made them — an ancestor, not modern humans.

climax.text: Group hunting requires coordination, planning, and communication. Weapon design implies language existed very early.

punchline.text: They designed balanced throwing weapons 400,000 years ago.

quiz.question: What is remarkable about the Schöningen spears?
options: They are the oldest metal weapons ever found
They were balanced for throwing, 200,000 years before Homo sapiens existed
They were made from a stone material not found in Germany

details.summary: Prehistoric hunting evolved from scavenging to sophisticated strategies using wooden spears, traps, and coordinated group drives. The Schöningen spears from Germany, dating to 300,000 years ago, prove that early humans were skilled hunters, not merely opportunistic scavengers.
details.whyItMatters: Hunting technology reveals cognitive sophistication — planning ambushes, crafting weapons, and coordinating group action. The Schöningen spears pushed back the timeline for complex hunting behavior by hundreds of thousands of years.
takeaways: The Schöningen spears date to 300,000 years ago in Germany
They prove early humans were skilled, planned hunters
Hunting required coordination, planning, and weapon crafting

faq.question: What do the Schöningen spears tell us?
faq.answer: They are expertly crafted with the weight balanced for throwing, like modern javelins. Found alongside butchered horse bones, they prove that humans 300,000 years ago were active hunters using sophisticated weapons, not just scavengers picking over carcasses.

faq.question: When did humans start hunting large animals?
faq.answer: Evidence for large-game hunting goes back at least 500,000 years, with increasing sophistication over time. Earlier hominins likely combined scavenging with opportunistic hunting before developing the weapons and strategies needed for reliable large-game hunting.
